summary: A companion app can materially lower the cost of system comprehension when it unifies static, runtime, and decision evidence. It should be treated as a derived interface with explicit provenance, never as an unqualified second source of truth.

points.text: Every claim, diagram element, metric, and decision should link to its source artifact or query, generation time, and source revision. Without provenance, a polished view obscures uncertainty.

Layered navigation should follow real comprehension questions: system boundary, component responsibility, dependency, runtime behavior, recent change, and rationale. A graph of everything is not a useful information architecture.
Static intent and observed runtime behavior must be visually distinct. Disagreement is valuable drift evidence and should not be reconciled by silently choosing whichever source is newer.
Effectiveness should be measured with task time, answer correctness, source navigation, and stale-claim rate; page views and aesthetic preference do not establish better comprehension.
